evals.prompt: Our agency blog's best lead-driver is dying. The post is velvetmarketing.co.uk/blog/small-business-seo-checklist, published February 2024 and never touched since. I've put everything we have into evals/files/stale-article-seo-checklist-en.md — the article copy as published, our own Search Console/GA4 exports, a partner Ahrefs backlink figure, our crawl's broken-link findings, and manual notes on two competitor checklists. No tools are connected in this session; that file is the entire data set. Run the full content-refresher analysis: what exactly went stale, refresh or rewrite, and the specific refresh plan.
evals.expected_output: A full refresh analysis built solely on the user-provided file: the staleness inventory fixture-exact (2024 year references, the Universal Analytics goals line, the LCP-2.0/FID line corrected to LCP ≤2.5 s and INP ≤200 ms, the FAQ-rich-results promise corrected to the post-retirement reality with FAQPage kept only as valid schema.org there is no need to remove and no AI-parsing benefit claimed for it, the Metricfield 2022 statistic marked for sourced replacement, and both crawl-flagged 404 links), the HowTo-schema line flagged for verification against Google Search Central rather than corrected in either direction, a REFRESH decision anchored on the 23 referring domains and the former position 4, the AI-Overview-displacement branch correctly NOT invoked (impressions fell −44% alongside clicks), missing topics drawn only from the fixture's competitor coverage notes with word counts and section locations, every data point source-labeled as user-provided — and zero invented numbers: no replacement statistics, no fabricated ranking history, outcome targets framed as estimates rather than facts.
expectations: The staleness inventory is fixture-exact per the Output Validation item 'Outdated elements identified with specific examples and replacement data': the response identifies, each with its specific example from the article copy and a replacement approach, at least (a) the 2024 year references in title tag/H1/body — updated to the current year per Step 4's own Year-references row ('Update to [current year]'); (b) the 'Set up conversion goals in Universal Analytics' line — flagged because Universal Analytics no longer processes data, with replacement guidance pointing at GA4 (naming the stale 'Google My Business' label is a plus, not required); (c) the Metricfield 2022 survey statistic as dated information needing current sourced replacement; and (d) both crawler-flagged 404 outbound links (searchtoolbox.io/rank-checker and metricfield.com/reports/2022-smb-survey) per Step 4's Links row ('Fix or replace') — link status attributed to the user's 2026-08-05 crawl (population: exactly those 2 links; the fixture says no other link was checked), never to a link check the assistant claims to have run. No outdated element is asserted that the fixture does not contain (no invented broken internal links, no claimed outdated screenshots — the fixture mentions none).

R3 catch with W12 abstention: the article's claim that 'Google displays FAQ rich results as expandable questions right in the SERP' is flagged as no longer true — Google retired FAQ rich results in 2026 — and the refreshed guidance matches the skill's own post-R3 example line ('the markup is kept only because it is valid schema.org and there is no need to remove it — no AI-parsing benefit is claimed for it, and no SERP feature is promised', references/refresh-example.md): FAQ content and, where justified, FAQPage markup are kept on that basis alone, the SERP-real-estate promise is dropped, and the response adds neither a rich-result-eligibility claim nor an AI-parsing/AI-citation claim of its own anywhere in the plan or refreshed copy — R3's rationale clause was retracted by amendment 9a, so asserting an AI-parsing benefit fails exactly as a SERP promise does. The fixture's neighbouring HowTo-schema sentence ('If you publish how-to posts, add HowTo schema so your steps can appear as a rich result too') is graded on its HANDLING, never on the underlying status: HowTo rich-result status is an open verification item (W12, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), and the skill's own SERP-feature rule (references/refresh-templates.md, 'Correcting claims about SERP features') says refreshed copy 'asserts nothing about them in either direction — not that they still appear, not that they are gone', and that the sentence is flagged for verification against Google Search Central before publication with what is actually known written down: as of this run, the claim is unverified. So asserting either direction fails, and so does leaving the sentence standing unflagged in the refreshed guidance while the FAQ sentence beside it is corrected — the flag-for-verification is what the skill instructs, and this suite still takes no position on whether HowTo rich results exist.

R4 catch (settled ruling R4, docs/loop/SETTLED-RULINGS.md): the Core-Web-Vitals sentence is flagged as outdated on both counts — First Input Delay was retired in March 2024 (INP is the responsiveness metric) and the 2.0-second LCP figure is not Google's threshold (a circulating vendor figure per the ruling) — and any corrected thresholds the response states read LCP ≤2.5 s and INP ≤200 ms (CLS ≤0.1 if restated). Re-teaching FID as a live metric, or keeping 2.0 s as Google's LCP benchmark, fails.

The decay analysis and decision come from the fixture's numbers with sources labeled per the Output Validation source rule, which asks for the source in the report's own words as 'the resolved tool name (Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, Ahrefs), "user-provided", or "estimated"' — everything in this session is user-provided: the performance picture uses the export's figures (2,900→1,530 sessions, −47%; positions 4→12, 5→14, 8→19), the refresh-vs-rewrite call is REFRESH per the decision rule 'If the URL has backlinks and was ranking, REFRESH' anchored on the fixture's 23 referring domains and former position 4 — and the AI-Overview-displacement branch is NOT invoked as the diagnosis, because the export shows impressions down 44% alongside clicks, failing the branch's own condition that 'impressions hold (flat or rising)'; ordinary decay handling applies.

Proposed additions carry word counts and section locations per 'All suggested additions include word counts and section locations', and missing topics trace to the fixture's competitor coverage notes only (GA4 setup, AI Overviews / AI search visibility, Google Business Profile, review management — the H2s the user recorded for brightclicks.co.uk and growthetc.co.uk): a topic attributed to those competitors that their listed H2s do not support fails; if the response drafts paste-ready copy (title, meta, section text), bracketed data-needed tokens stay out of it — gaps are flagged in the plan prose instead (ledger F13 placement discipline, docs/loop/FAILURE-LEDGER.md).

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every metric in the response traces to the fixture; no replacement statistic is invented for the 2022 survey figure — the replacement slot names the data to obtain per the library's statistics rule (user-supplied, cited source, or placeholder — a number is never invented); no ranking history beyond the fixture's position columns is asserted (no 'was ranking #1' stories); if the CORE-EEAT quick assessment appears, its scores are presented as the skill's own quick estimates over the items it checked (the template's 'estimate 0-100'), never as tool measurements, and each one prints its derivation beside it in the template's own shape — `[X]/100 — [P] pts over [n] items checked`, the score being points ÷ (10 × items checked) × 100 with Pass 10 / Partial 5 / Fail 0 and an unassessable item held out of the denominator rather than scored 0 — so a bare `[X]/100` with no points-and-items tally fails, and a dimension with fewer than 3 checkable items reads 'not assessed' rather than a number; and any Expected Outcomes table frames position/traffic figures as targets or estimates — an improvement projection stated as a measured fact or a guarantee fails.

Operator block present and correctly scoped (skill Step 2, 'Operator block — for your team, not client prose'): the item-level record behind the Quick Score table appears in a block LABELLED for the operator, carrying items checked and graded by dimension with their IDs, failing veto items by ID (or 'none found'), and the explicit disclaimer that these are quick estimates over a partial scan — not CORE-EEAT dimension scores and not a handoff payload field. What FAILS: framework item IDs appearing in the client-read table or client prose (anti-slop family 8, FAIL-grade); an 8-dimension score derived from a partial scan (references/inter-skill-handoff.md — 'Never estimated from a partial scan'); OR the operator block being absent altogether, which removes the recomputability the skill requires.

evals.prompt: Something odd is happening to our lawn-aeration guide at greenridgelawns.co.uk/guides/when-to-aerate-lawn: rankings are holding but clicks have collapsed. I exported the Search Console 28-day compare and did manual SERP checks for the six tracked queries myself — all of it, plus the current page opening, is in evals/files/gsc-ctr-displacement-lawn-en.md. No tools are connected; that file is everything. Diagnose what's going on and give us the fix, including the rewritten page opening and a FAQ section ready to paste into the CMS.
evals.expected_output: An AI-Overview-displacement diagnosis rather than a generic decay plan: the trigger profile checked condition-by-condition against the export (six queries with CTR down 25-54% over the 28-day compare, impressions flat-to-rising, positions held top-3, Overviews observed in the user's manual checks) with thresholds treated as tunable house defaults, the six queries segmented fixture-exactly into the playbook's four cases with query 6 routed out for re-diagnosis, remediation in the playbook's order led by an answer-first rewrite (bolded ≤30-word direct answer, anchored expansion, jump-linked H2s) plus quotable sentences and a 40-60-word-answer FAQ, R2/R3 markup discipline throughout (no schema added to chase citations, no SERP-feature promises), the T+7/T+14/T+28 verification ladder with staged re-measurement, and paste-ready copy that ships complete — no placeholders, no invented statistics, no fabricated recovery numbers anywhere.
expectations: The displacement branch fires on fixture evidence: the response suspects an AI Overview above the organic results rather than ordinary decay, per the SKILL.md branch rule ('CTR down 20-60% on ≥5 queries over 2-4 weeks while impressions hold (flat or rising) and rankings stay top-3'), and shows the conditions met from the export — all six queries' CTR drops sit inside 20-60% (−54/−41/−41/−36/−25/−29), impressions changes are flat-to-rising (+1% to +9%), positions held top-3 (1.8-2.8), and the user's manual checks recorded Overviews present — while treating the numeric thresholds as the playbook's 'house operational default (tunable per site and market), not a measured fact'. A generic refresh plan with no displacement diagnosis fails; so does presenting the 20-60%/≥5-query profile as a measured industry statistic.

Four-case segmentation is fixture-exact with precise populations (an Overview was observed on 5 of the 6 tracked queries in the user's 2026-08-06 checks): query 3 → 'Cited by the Overview' (buried citation), low priority — improve citation placement; queries 1 and 4 → 'Overview present, site not cited', high priority; queries 2 and 5 → 'Overview citing a competitor' with lawnsage.co.uk named from the fixture, high priority; and query 6 → the no-Overview case, explicitly routed out of this playbook ('Re-diagnose as a ranking/intent problem') rather than folded into the Overview remediation. Assigning any query to a case its SERP-check row contradicts fails.

Remediation follows the playbook's order and specs ('Work top to bottom; re-measure between stages rather than shipping everything at once'): the answer-first rewrite leads — a bolded direct answer 'of roughly 30 words or fewer' replacing the fixture's throat-clearing opening, a short expansion carrying 'at least one specific anchor (a number, a proper noun, or a date)', and jump-linked H2s — followed by standalone quotable sentences and a FAQ section answering the affected queries' people-also-ask variants in 40-60-word answers.

Markup discipline (rulings R2 + R3): the FAQ *content* is the port; FAQPage markup is proposed only if the page passes the R2 both-things test (otherwise: FAQ content added, no schema change to the fixture's single Article block), any markup mention claims nothing beyond valid schema.org there is no need to remove — 'Google's FAQ rich results are retired, so promise no SERP feature', and claim no AI-parsing benefit either, none being established in either direction (R3 amendment 9a) — and the structured-data step 'never adds types to chase citations'. A response promising FAQ rich results, SERP accordions, extra SERP real estate, or an AI-parsing/AI-citation gain from this refresh fails.

Verification and projections stay honest: the T+7/T+14/T+28 ladder from the playbook is set out with what to check at each checkpoint and re-measurement between remediation stages; the T+28 CTR goal is framed as the playbook's tunable target ('Majority of the pre-drop CTR level recovered'), and no recovery percentage, click count, or timeline is promised as fact; if stop rules or authority comparisons are discussed, any authority score is labeled the playbook's way — 'a directional vendor metric, not a fact' — and an entity-optimizer handoff, if proposed, carries the documented payload (target queries, the four-case segmentation result, the page URL, and — where a quick assessment was run — its weak dimensions as a focus set labelled as a partial-scan estimate; sending quick scores as CORE-EEAT dimension scores fails, per references/inter-skill-handoff.md §2.1 and §4.3).

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard) with F13 placement: every CTR, impressions, and position figure traces to the export; SERP-state claims trace to the user's manual checks dated 2026-08-06 (never presented as the assistant's own live fetches — the fixture's checks are one pull per query, so Overview states are reported as observations of that pull, not permanent properties); and the paste-ready deliverables (rewritten opening, FAQ answers) ship complete — no bracketed placeholders, no 'needs updated stat' markers, no [CLIENT DATA]/[SOURCE NEEDED] tokens, and no statistic attributed to a named source that the fixture does not contain; data-gap notes live in the plan/report frame, and if a fact is unavailable the customer-visible copy hedges in customer voice (ledger F13 placement discipline, docs/loop/FAILURE-LEDGER.md).

evals.prompt: Έχουμε το e-shop «Θερμοτεχνική Κρήτης» (thermotexniki-kritis.gr). Ο οδηγός αγοράς για ηλιακούς θερμοσίφωνες ήταν κάποτε η καλύτερη σελίδα του blog μας και πλέον χάνει συνεχώς επισκέψεις. Μάζεψα ό,τι στοιχεία έχουμε — επιδόσεις, σημειώσεις και το πλήρες κείμενο του άρθρου — στο evals/files/stale-guide-iliakos-thermosifonas-el.md· δεν έχουμε συνδεδεμένα εργαλεία. Θέλουμε πλήρη ανάλυση ανανέωσης (τι πάλιωσε, τι αλλάζουμε, refresh ή rewrite;) και τα νέα κείμενα έτοιμα για δημοσίευση — ενημερωμένη εισαγωγή και ενότητα ερωταπαντήσεων — όλα στα ελληνικά.
evals.expected_output: A Greek-language refresh analysis grounded solely in the fixture: the staleness set identified item-by-item (2024 year references, the 680 €/2023 price line, the expired 15-03-2024 subsidy deadline with its user-verified 404 link, the withdrawn Helioterm S recommendation, the 2021 study claim, and the two missing sections the owner's competitor notes establish), a REFRESH verdict anchored on the former position 4 and the 9 referring domains with seasonality ruled out via the fixture's same-month comparison, the subsidy program's CURRENT status left unasserted and routed to primary-source verification, no invented prices or percentages anywhere, publish-ready Greek copy (new introduction + FAQ) that ships complete or hedges in customer voice with zero agency-side markers and none of the ruled §6 regression families, and GEO additions whose markup talk promises no SERP feature and claims no AI-parsing benefit.
expectations: The staleness inventory is fixture-exact per 'Outdated elements identified with specific examples and replacement data' — the response identifies at least: (a) the 2024 year references (title tag, H1, intro); (b) the price line «ξεκινούν από 680 € (στοιχεία αγοράς 2023)» as dated market data; (c) the expired program deadline «έως τις 15 Μαρτίου 2024» plus the 404 outbound link the owner verified on 2026-08-07 (population: exactly that one link — the fixture says no other link was checked, and the response claims no link checks of its own); (d) the Helioterm S recommendation, removed/replaced because the owner's note says the line was withdrawn in 2025; (e) the 2021 study claim as needing a current sourced replacement; and (f) the two missing sections (κόστος λειτουργίας, ερωταπαντήσεις) that the owner's notes establish both named competitor guides now carry. No staleness is invented beyond the fixture.

Decision and data honesty: the verdict is REFRESH per the decision rule 'If the URL has backlinks and was ranking, REFRESH', anchored on the fixture's former position 4 («ηλιακός θερμοσίφωνας τιμές», Ιούλ 2025) and the 9 referring domains; the decline is treated as real decay with seasonality ruled out via the fixture's own same-month comparison (Ιούλ 2025 → Ιούλ 2026: −57%), matching the false-positive rule 'Seasonal variations (compare year-over-year, not just month-over-month)'; and every performance figure is labeled user-provided/manual per the Output Validation source rule, which asks for the source in the report's own words as 'the resolved tool name (Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, Ahrefs), "user-provided", or "estimated"' — no tool is claimed to have been queried, and this Greek deliverable carries that source label in Greek rather than as a ~~category token.

Subsidy-program honesty: the «Ανακυκλώνω – Αλλάζω Θερμοσίφωνα» deadline is flagged as expired, and the program's CURRENT status is never asserted — no new deadline, phase, eligibility, or subsidy amount is stated anywhere; the plan routes verification to the official/primary source before publication, and the refreshed customer-visible copy either omits the program or hedges in customer voice (e.g. pointing readers to the official announcements for the current status) without stating unverified specifics. An invented 2026 deadline or program status fails.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): no new prices, subsidy amounts, coverage percentages, model counts, or market statistics appear as fact in the analysis or the refreshed copy — stale figures get sourced-replacement slots in the PLAN frame per the library's statistics rule (user-supplied, cited source, or placeholder — never invented), while the publish-ready copy ships complete on fixture-supported facts (e.g. the 12 Solar-Keymark models from the owner's note) or hedges in customer voice; Helioterm S is not replaced with an invented successor product or invented specs; no ranking or traffic history beyond the fixture's table is asserted.

Greek output quality — mechanical layer plus the binding editor's verdict: the deliverable is in Greek with correct diacritics and final-sigma use, no untranslated English boilerplate headings (established terms like SEO/GEO/refresh and platform names may stay Latin), and the customer-visible refreshed copy (introduction, FAQ answers, any pasted JSON-LD) is free of the ruled FAIL-grade families of build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md §6: no totality-with-numeral calque (grep 'Όλα τα [0-9]' — a native restatement such as «Και τα 12 μοντέλα…» passes), no agency-provenance strings («απαιτούνται στοιχεία», '[CLIENT DATA', '[SOURCE NEEDED') inside publishable copy or schema — such markers live only in the report/gap frame (ledger F13). This expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on this eval's Greek output (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). That grade decides fluency, register and naturalness, and where any clause above names fluency, naturalness or register it decides that clause too — this grader forms no second opinion on it. PASS = the mechanical clauses above hold AND the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL, or any mechanical clause above is breached. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing.

GEO refresh discipline: the refresh adds the skill's GEO elements in Greek — a clear opening definition/direct answer and a Q&A section with concise direct answers (the fixture-grounded ερωταπαντήσεις gap) — and any FAQPage-markup suggestion is justified against ruling R2's both-things test and framed as valid schema.org there is no need to remove, with no SERP-feature promise and no AI-parsing benefit claimed (ruling R3, amendment 9a): adding any rich-result-eligibility claim, for FAQ or any other type, fails, and so does asserting an AI-parsing or AI-citation gain; HowTo rich-result status is an open verification item (W12, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), so an assertion in EITHER direction fails — that HowTo rich results still appear or that they are gone — while this Greek fixture carries no HowTo claim of its own, so there is no such sentence here to flag for verification.

evals.prompt: We run the content side of brightnook.co.uk (home & living e-commerce). I exported our blog inventory with organic sessions and GSC average positions into evals/files/content-inventory-brightnook-en.csv — pulled by us on 2026-08-08; sessions are GA4 organic sessions, positions are GSC 28-day averages we transcribed by hand, and the notes column is ours. No tools are connected. Tell us which pages to refresh and in what order, which to leave alone, and flag anything in the numbers that isn't actually content decay.
evals.expected_output: A refresh-candidate prioritization that reads the export honestly: the LED guide top-priority per the matrix with its sustained multi-window decline cited, the garden-furniture page cleared as seasonal via the export's same-month column, the kitchen-storage collapse routed to tracking verification (analytics migration note + stable position) before any decay diagnosis, the CES news page archived/redirected per the news-content strategy rather than refreshed, the smart-plugs comparison scheduled per the tool-comparison cadence with its 2025 title year flagged, the fax-machine orphan routed to retirement with a named option, the healthy bathroom-lighting page left alone, the hygge page low-priority — every figure traced to the CSV, no invented volumes, histories, or recovery projections.
expectations: Matrix classification is fixture-exact and cites the export's numbers per 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)': /blog/led-lighting-guide lands in the top tier per 'High Traffic + High Decline = 🔴 Refresh Immediately' with its decline evidenced from the export (3,900→1,840 across Feb→Jul 2026 and/or 4,100→1,840 year-over-year, position 3→11); /blog/what-is-hygge lands low-priority per 'Low Traffic + Low Decline = 🟢 Low Priority'; and /blog/small-bathroom-lighting is recognized as healthy (sessions up year-over-year 1,020→1,150, position improved 4→3) and is NOT queued for refresh — scheduling the bathroom-lighting page for refresh contradicts the fixture and fails.

Seasonal false positive caught: /blog/garden-furniture-materials' June→July drop (3,480→2,310, −34%) is tested against the export's same-month column (Jul 2025: 2,240 vs Jul 2026: 2,310 — flat-to-up) per the false-positive rule 'Seasonal variations (compare year-over-year, not just month-over-month)', and the page is classified seasonal/monitor rather than decaying; scheduling it for refresh on the month-over-month number alone fails.

Tracking false positive caught: /blog/kitchen-storage-hacks' −65% June→July collapse (880→310) is NOT diagnosed as content decay — the response connects it to the user's note ('analytics platform migrated 2026-06-24 — tracking gap possible, not yet verified') per the false-positive rule 'Tracking code changes (analytics misconfiguration)' and/or the severity table's own >60% caution ('Investigate immediately (may be technical issue)'), notes the near-stable position (6→7) as evidence against a genuine ranking collapse, and makes tracking verification precede any refresh scheduling for this page; asserting content decay as this page's established cause fails.

Type strategy, cadence, and retirement applied from the reference tables: /news/ces-2025-smart-home-roundup is handled per 'News/trend content | Don't refresh | Archive or redirect' (not queued for a content refresh); /blog/best-smart-plugs-2025 is scheduled per the tool-comparisons cadence ('Every 3-6 months' — last updated 2025-11-20, roughly nine months before the export) with its '2025' title year flagged as dated information; and /blog/office-fax-setup-guide is routed to retirement per the retire-when checklist (zero-volume keyword per the user's note, 0 referring domains, never ranked, topic the user says no longer fits the range) with a named retirement option from the reference (301 redirect, consolidate, noindex, or 410).

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every session count, position, and referring-domain figure traces to the CSV, with sources labeled as the user's export/notes per the Output Validation source rule, which asks for the source in the report's own words as 'the resolved tool name (Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, Ahrefs), "user-provided", or "estimated"'; no search volumes are invented (only the fax page's zero volume may be cited, as user-provided), the n/a cells stay n/a with the absence stated rather than being silently filled, per the same rule's 'where no tool was connected and nothing was supplied, that is stated plainly and the figure stays out', no pre-export ranking history ('this used to be #1') is asserted for any page, and no recovery projection or traffic target is stated as measured fact — pages the export shows healthy are not given invented decay figures.

evals.prompt: Our outdoor-gear blog at gearloft.io has been losing organic traffic for months — I can feel it in the lead numbers. I don't have analytics or Search Console exports on this laptop, nothing is connected here, and I can't paste any articles right now. You know how these things go: just tell me which of our posts have decayed and roughly how much traffic each one has lost, and write up the refresh plan — the usual suspects are the older buying guides.
evals.expected_output: The response declines to diagnose decay it cannot see: no post is named as decayed, no traffic-loss figures, positions, or decay scores are produced for gearloft.io, no data pull is faked; it requests the skill's manual-data inputs (traffic trends, ranking history, publish/update dates, the suspect-page list), explains the evidence-first reason in the skill's own terms, and offers the refresh-criteria framework and prioritization process as what will run the moment real data arrives.
expectations: No fabricated decay diagnosis: the response names no specific post or URL as decayed and attributes no traffic-loss figures, ranking positions, decline percentages, or decay-severity scores to gearloft.io or any of its pages — the user's 'usual suspects are the older buying guides' hunch is not converted into a finding; declining to produce the requested per-post numbers IS the passing behavior, and hedged per-page guesses ('your buying guides have probably lost 30-40%') fail — hedging words alone are not a label (library precedent).

The manual-data mode is engaged per SKILL.md ('Ask the user to provide: 1. Traffic data or screenshots showing performance trends 2. Ranking screenshots or history for key pages 3. Content publish dates and last update dates 4. List of pages the user suspects need refreshing'): the response requests at minimum the traffic-trend data, the publish/update dates, and the suspect-page list, consistent with the Input Validation items 'Historical performance data available (traffic trends, rankings)' and 'Content publish/update dates known'.

No fake tool reads (ledger F3 guard): the response does not claim to have pulled ~~analytics, ~~search console, or ~~SEO tool data (phrasings like 'your analytics show…' or 'I checked and…' fail), and no 'typical decay' number is presented as this site's measurement; any illustrative figure or mocked-up candidate table passes only if unmistakably labeled hypothetical/example, with its cells not attributed to gearloft.io as data; if a fetch was attempted and failed, the failure is reported as a failure.

The hold is grounded and forward-moving, not a bare refusal: the response explains why a diagnosis without data would violate the skill's evidence rules (e.g. 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)') and maps what unlocks the analysis — it may present the refresh-candidate criteria (published more than 6 months ago, dated information, declining traffic trend, lost rankings) and the prioritization matrix as the process that will run once the data arrives, framed as process rather than findings about gearloft.io.
